_about: Graphics quality tiers, the AUTO tier's start-up pick and the frame-time governor (app/quality.rs). tiers: the 3D render-target scale of each tier (the share of the window it renders at; LOW 0.35, MEDIUM 0.40 and HIGH 0.50 are the shipped look; LOW was 0.25 until 2026-11-12, when KT asked for a sharper picture on low-end machines). notches: what the governor gives up, one row per step, notch 0 first; a row's numbers are factors of the tier's own setting (render_scale: of its render scale; lamps: the most lamps the shader lights with, 16, 8 or 4; cull_scale: of the fog cull distance; prop_scale: of the draw distance of props drawn one by one; stream_scale: of the per-frame chunk build budget). Notch 0 must be the tier as it is (all 1 and 16 lamps) and no row may ask for more than the row before it. governor (a port of Godot's quality_governor.gd): it watches a rolling average of the frame time over window_seconds against 1000 / target_fps (capped by the FPS LIMIT row). Over target x miss_factor for miss_seconds it gives up one notch (at most one per down_cooldown); at or under target x ok_factor for up_seconds it takes one back, unless a hold is running. A step down within bounce_window seconds of a step up is a bounce: it holds the next step up for bounce_hold seconds, doubling per consecutive bounce up to bounce_max times, and the escalation is forgotten after stable_forget seconds of calm. A frame of stall_ms or more is a load or a stall, not a steady-state shortfall, and is not fed. auto: the AUTO tier is picked once. hardware: the first row whose conditions all hold names the tier (gpu_contains: any of these words in the GPU name the browser reports (hw.js key gpu, the WebGL unmasked renderer, compared in upper case, so an Intel HD 6000 MacBook Air starts on LOW without waiting for frames); max_cores / max_memory_gb: the browser's hardwareConcurrency / deviceMemory, both only when the browser reports them; mobile and software: true or false). default_tier is used when nothing matches; unknown_tier when the browser reported nothing at all. Then the first play seconds are measured: settle_seconds of play are skipped, the next measure_seconds are timed (at least min_frames frames), and a median frame time over low_above_ratio times the target frame time picks LOW, over medium_above_ratio picks MEDIUM; the AUTO tier is the lower of that and the hardware tier. A native build has no hardware report and keeps AUTO = HIGH. The governor runs only on AUTO, and only while the ADAPTIVE QUALITY setting is on.
